ledger.why: the casting line (the roles carry it)

collection.description: A villager is asked about the oldest thing they own, and fetches a small, chipped clay cup.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Sitting outside after dinner, (friend) asks a question out of nowhere: "What's the oldest thing you own?" (subject) has to think. Then (subject.he/she) goes into (subject.his/her) hut and comes back with a small, chipped clay cup that (subject.he/she) has had for as long as (subject.he/she) can remember. Nobody knows who made it. It has always just been there.

choices.label: Wonder About Who Had It Before

a.name: Answer A
a.text: (subject) tells (friend) everything (subject.he/she) knows about the cup, which isn't much: it was in the hut when (subject.he/she) was small, it got chipped the year of the big storm, and once (subject.he/she) dropped it and it bounced. (friend) goes and fetches (friend.his/her) own oldest thing, a worn wooden comb. They spend the evening trading stories about two very ordinary, very old objects, and both of them hold their things a little more carefully afterward.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (subject) turns the cup over in (subject.his/her) hands. Somebody made it. Somebody drank from it, long before (subject) was born. Maybe lots of somebodies. (friend) and (subject) make up a few of them: a fisher who liked very hot tea, a child who used it to catch frogs. None of it is true, probably. The cup doesn't seem to mind.
